questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with stable angina takes a sublingual nitroglycerin tablet during an episode of exertional chest pain, and his symptoms resolve within minutes. Which of the following best describes the primary mechanism by which this drug relieves his chest pain?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It antagonizes beta-adrenergic receptors on the myocardium

choices.label: B
choices.text: It blocks L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle

choices.label: C
choices.text: It increases heart rate and contractility to improve perfusion

choices.label: D
choices.text: It inhibits platelet aggregation within the coronary arteries

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is converted to nitric oxide

explanation.summary: Nitrates are converted to nitric oxide, which activates guanylyl cyclase and raises cGMP to relax vascular smooth muscle.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the body, nitrates are converted to nitric oxide (NO). NO activates guanylyl cyclase, which increases cGMP and causes relaxation (dilation) of vascular smooth muscle. This vasodilation is the basis for the anti-anginal effect of nitrates.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Beta-blockade is not the mechanism of nitrates and is not described in the brick.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Calcium-channel blockade is the mechanism of a different drug class; nitrates act through the NO/cGMP pathway.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nitrates reduce cardiac workload; they do not primarily increase heart rate and contractility.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The brick attributes the anti-anginal effect to vasodilation, not to antiplatelet action.

questions.topicName: Nitrates

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman is treated with nitroglycerin for angina. The drug reduces her myocardial oxygen demand. Which of the following effects most directly accounts for this reduction in oxygen demand?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A reflex increase in myocardial contraction force

choices.label: B
choices.text: An increase in heart rate to improve tissue perfusion

choices.label: C
choices.text: An increase in systemic vascular resistance

choices.label: D
choices.text: Constriction of the coronary arteries

choices.label: E
choices.text: Dilation of the large veins returning to the heart

explanation.summary: Nitrate-induced venodilation lowers the work of the heart and reduces myocardial oxygen use.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that relaxation (dilation) of the large veins that return to the heart decreases contraction force, increases blood flow, and reduces myocardial oxygen use. Lowering the workload of the heart in this way decreases its oxygen demand and relieves ischemic chest pain.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nitrates decrease contraction force; they do not reflexively increase it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Increasing heart rate would raise, not lower, myocardial oxygen demand.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nitrates cause vasodilation and lower vascular resistance rather than increasing it.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nitrates dilate coronary arteries; they do not constrict them.

questions.topicName: Nitrates

questions.stem: In addition to reducing the heart's oxygen demand, nitrates relieve angina through an effect that increases oxygen supply to the myocardium. Which of the following best describes this additional effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An increase in blood hemoglobin concentration

choices.label: B
choices.text: Constriction of peripheral veins to raise coronary perfusion pressure

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct coronary artery vasodilation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dissolution of atherosclerotic plaque within the coronary arteries

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stimulation of new coronary vessel growth

explanation.summary: Nitrates also cause direct coronary artery vasodilation, increasing oxygen supply to the heart.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beyond lowering oxygen demand through venodilation, the brick notes that nitrates cause some direct coronary artery vasodilation that increases oxygen supply to the heart, further relieving chest pain.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nitrates do not raise hemoglobin concentration.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nitrates dilate veins rather than constricting them, and venoconstriction is not their mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nitrates relieve symptoms by vasodilation; they do not dissolve plaque.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nitrates act acutely by dilating existing vessels, not by growing new ones.

questions.topicName: Nitrates

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man develops acute substernal chest pain in the emergency department. He is given a nitroglycerin tablet to place under his tongue. Which of the following best explains why the sublingual route is preferred for acute angina?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It automatically provides a built-in nitrate-free interval

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is effective only for chronic angina, not acute episodes

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is rapidly absorbed and avoids first-pass hepatic metabolism

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is slowly absorbed, providing sustained drug levels over many hours

choices.label: E
choices.text: It undergoes extensive first-pass metabolism before reaching the circulation

explanation.summary: Sublingual nitroglycerin is absorbed rapidly and bypasses first-pass metabolism, giving fast relief of acute angina.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that sublingual nitroglycerin tablets are the most common form: placed under the tongue, they avoid first-pass metabolism, are rapidly absorbed, and can quickly relieve angina. This makes them ideal for acute episodes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A nitrate-free interval is a deliberate dosing strategy, not an inherent feature of a single sublingual tablet.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sublingual nitroglycerin is a short-acting agent used for acute angina.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Slow, sustained absorption describes oral agents like isosorbide mononitrate, not sublingual nitroglycerin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Avoiding first-pass metabolism is precisely the advantage of the sublingual route.

questions.topicName: Nitrates

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with chronic stable angina is prescribed a nitrate that is swallowed as an oral tablet, is slowly absorbed, and undergoes first-pass metabolism. Which of the following agents is he most likely taking?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Intravenous nitroglycerin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Isosorbide mononitrate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sodium nitroprusside

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sublingual nitroglycerin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Translingual nitroglycerin spray

explanation.summary: Oral isosorbide mononitrate is slowly absorbed, undergoes first-pass metabolism, and is used for chronic angina.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick describes isosorbide mononitrate as a delayed-release tablet that is swallowed, slowly absorbed, and undergoes first-pass metabolism. Despite this, it produces the same vasodilation effects and is used for chronic angina.

whyWrongByChoice.A: IV nitroglycerin is given intravenously and bypasses first-pass metabolism, and it is short-acting for acute use.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sodium nitroprusside is an IV short-acting agent, not an oral tablet.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sublingual nitroglycerin is placed under the tongue and avoids first-pass metabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Translingual nitroglycerin is a spray applied to the tongue and is short-acting for acute angina.

questions.topicName: Nitrates

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman with severe chest pain has received repeated doses of sublingual nitroglycerin, but her pain keeps returning after each dose wears off. The physician applies a transdermal nitroglycerin patch to her chest. Which property of the patch makes it useful in this situation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It avoids all systemic absorption, acting only locally on the skin

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is indicated exclusively for chronic angina and never for acute pain

choices.label: C
choices.text: It works by a mechanism unrelated to nitric oxide

choices.label: D
choices.text: Its delayed onset and slower absorption through the skin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Its immediate onset makes it faster than sublingual tablets

explanation.summary: Transdermal nitroglycerin has a delayed onset and is more slowly absorbed, giving a continuous effect useful for persistent, late acute angina.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick explains that nitroglycerin ointment and the transdermal patch have a delayed onset because of transdermal absorption. This makes them useful for late acute angina: rather than repeatedly re-dosing sublingual nitroglycerin, applying a patch provides a continuous effect as the drug is more slowly absorbed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The patch is absorbed transdermally into the circulation to produce systemic vasodilation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: In this clinical scenario the patch is used for continuing (late) acute angina, not only chronic angina.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Like all nitrates, the patch works through conversion to nitric oxide.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The patch has a delayed, not immediate, onset; sublingual tablets act faster.

questions.topicName: Nitrates

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man is started on nitroglycerin for angina. Which of the following is the most common adverse effect he is likely to experience?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bradycardia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Constipation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dry cough

choices.label: D
choices.text: Headache

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hypertension

explanation.summary: Headache is the most common adverse effect of nitrates.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that the most common adverse effect of nitrates is headache, reported by more than 60% of patients who receive nitroglycerin. It is thought to result from the rapid vasodilation nitroglycerin produces, and is notably less common with long-acting isosorbide mononitrate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bradycardia is not described as a nitrate adverse effect in the brick.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Constipation is not a nitrate adverse effect discussed in the brick.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dry cough is associated with a different drug class, not nitrates.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nitrates cause vasodilation and hypotension, not hypertension.

questions.topicName: Nitrates

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man with a history of atherosclerosis develops chest pain when he walks uphill. His physician explains that his angina pectoris is caused by which of the following underlying processes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Excess oxygen supply to the myocardium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inflammation of the pericardial sac

choices.label: C
choices.text: Myocardial ischemia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Obstruction of a pulmonary artery by a thrombus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spasm of the lower esophageal sphincter

explanation.summary: Angina pectoris is chest pain caused by myocardial ischemia, a lack of oxygen reaching heart cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick defines angina pectoris as chest pain caused by myocardial ischemia (lack of oxygen leading toward cardiac cell death). Atherosclerosis reduces the effective diameter of blood vessels, lowering blood flow and oxygen delivery to the myocardium and producing the ischemic chest pain.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Angina results from insufficient, not excess, oxygen delivery to the heart.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pericardial inflammation is a different entity and is not the cause of angina described here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pulmonary embolism is a separate condition and is not the described cause of angina.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Esophageal spasm can mimic chest pain but is not the mechanism of angina pectoris.

questions.topicName: Nitrates

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man is receiving intravenous nitroglycerin. Which of the following adverse effects most specifically requires that his blood pressure be monitored regularly during this therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Headache

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hypotension

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nitrate tolerance

choices.label: D
choices.text: Peripheral edema

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reflex bradycardia

explanation.summary: IV nitrates cause significant vasodilation that can produce hypotension, so blood pressure must be monitored regularly.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick notes that IV nitroglycerin and sodium nitroprusside are used to acutely lower blood pressure, and the significant vasodilation they cause can produce hypotension. Any patient receiving nitrates should have blood pressure monitored regularly.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Headache is the most common adverse effect but is not the reason blood pressure is monitored.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Nitrate tolerance is a loss of drug effect over time, not an indication for blood-pressure monitoring.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Peripheral edema is not a nitrate adverse effect discussed in the brick.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reflex bradycardia is not the monitored concern described in the brick.

questions.topicName: Nitrates

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man whose angina is usually well controlled has now received continuous nitrate therapy for more than 14 hours without any nitrate-free period. His previously controlled chest pain has returned despite ongoing dosing. Which of the following best explains the loss of drug efficacy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A paradoxical reflex vasoconstriction caused by cGMP

choices.label: B
choices.text: An IgE-mediated allergic reaction to nitrates

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enhanced conversion of nitroglycerin to nitric oxide

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased first-pass metabolism raising active drug levels

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nitrate tolerance from sustained high-dose exposure

explanation.summary: Continuous exposure to high-dose nitrates causes tolerance (tachyphylaxis), attenuating their effect.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick teaches that frequently repeated or continuous exposure to high doses of nitrates leads to tolerance (tachyphylaxis), a marked attenuation of most of their pharmacological effects. After more than 14 hours of continuous nitrates without a nitrate-free interval, the returning chest pain reflects developing nitrate tolerance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: cGMP mediates vasodilation; a paradoxical reflex vasoconstriction from cGMP is not described.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The brick attributes the loss of effect to tolerance, not to an allergic (IgE-mediated) reaction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tolerance is associated with reduced, not enhanced, conversion of nitroglycerin to NO.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Increased active drug levels would enhance, not reduce, the effect.

questions.topicName: Nitrates

questions.stem: A physician wants to design a nitrate regimen that minimizes the development of tolerance in a patient on long-acting nitrate therapy. Which of the following strategies is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Administer the nitrate continuously without interruption

choices.label: B
choices.text: Give the drug every 4 hours without any break

choices.label: C
choices.text: Include a daily 10-12 hour nitrate-free interval

choices.label: D
choices.text: Steadily increase the dose over time

choices.label: E
choices.text: Switch the patient to intravenous dosing around the clock

explanation.summary: A daily 10-12 hour nitrate-free interval decreases the likelihood of nitrate tolerance.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that nitrate therapy should be designed to prevent tolerance, and that nitrates require a 10-12 hour nitrate-free interval to decrease the likelihood of tolerance and allow the return of efficacy. For example, a patch is worn for 12-14 hours and removed for 10-12 hours.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Continuous, uninterrupted dosing promotes tolerance rather than preventing it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Frequent dosing with no break provides continuous exposure, promoting tolerance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Increasing the dose does not prevent tolerance and can worsen adverse effects.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Around-the-clock IV dosing provides no nitrate-free interval and would encourage tolerance.

questions.topicName: Nitrates

questions.stem: A pharmacology student is asked to describe a proposed cellular mechanism underlying nitrate tolerance. Which of the following best fits what the brick describes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A reduced capacity to convert nitroglycerin to nitric oxide

choices.label: B
choices.text: An increase in intracellular cGMP production

choices.label: C
choices.text: Downregulation of beta-adrenergic receptors in the myocardium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enhanced first-pass metabolism that increases active drug delivery

choices.label: E
choices.text: Upregulation of guanylyl cyclase in vascular smooth muscle

explanation.summary: Nitrate tolerance may result from reduced ability of vascular smooth muscle to convert nitroglycerin to NO.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that the magnitude of tolerance is a function of dosage and frequency of use, and that tolerance may result from a reduced capacity of the vascular smooth muscle to convert nitroglycerin to NO (true vascular tolerance) or from activation of mechanisms extraneous to the vessel wall.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Increased cGMP would strengthen the response, the opposite of tolerance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Beta-receptor downregulation is unrelated to the nitrate NO/cGMP mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tolerance is a pharmacodynamic loss of effect at the vessel, not increased active drug delivery.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tolerance reflects a diminished vasodilatory response; upregulating guanylyl cyclase would enhance, not blunt, the effect.

questions.topicName: Nitrates

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with erectile dysfunction and no correctable underlying cause is started on sildenafil. Which of the following best describes the mechanism by which this drug improves erectile function?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It activates guanylyl cyclase to increase production of cGMP

choices.label: B
choices.text: It blocks phosphodiesterase type 5 and reduces the breakdown of cGMP

choices.label: C
choices.text: It directly causes vasoconstriction within the corpus cavernosum

choices.label: D
choices.text: It directly stimulates nitric oxide synthase in the vascular endothelium

choices.label: E
choices.text: It increases release of nitric oxide from penile smooth muscle

explanation.summary: PDE-5 inhibitors block the enzyme that degrades cGMP, prolonging smooth muscle relaxation and blood flow.
explanation.whyCorrect: Under normal circumstances PDE-5 degrades cGMP, which would decrease smooth muscle relaxation and blood flow. By blocking PDE-5, these drugs reduce cGMP breakdown, leading to prolonged smooth muscle dilation in response to nitric oxide and increased blood flow in the corpus cavernosum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Guanylyl cyclase is activated by nitric oxide, not by PDE-5 inhibitors; the drugs do not increase cGMP production.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The drugs promote vasodilation and increased blood flow, not vasoconstriction, in the corpus cavernosum.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PDE-5 inhibitors do not stimulate nitric oxide synthase; they act downstream on cGMP metabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PDE-5 inhibitors do not increase nitric oxide release; they prolong the effect of cGMP already generated by the NO pathway.

questions.topicName: PDE-5 Inhibitors

questions.stem: During the normal male sexual response, nitric oxide is released and activates an enzyme that converts GTP to cGMP, leading to smooth muscle relaxation. Which enzyme is directly activated by nitric oxide?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adenylyl cyclase

choices.label: B
choices.text: CYP3A4

choices.label: C
choices.text: Guanylyl cyclase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nitric oxide synthase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Phosphodiesterase type 5

explanation.summary: Nitric oxide activates guanylyl cyclase, which converts GTP to cGMP to relax smooth muscle.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick teaches that nitric oxide activates guanylyl cyclase, which converts GTP to cGMP; the net result is relaxation of smooth muscle and increased blood flow needed for an erection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adenylyl cyclase generates cAMP, not cGMP, and is not the target of nitric oxide here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CYP3A4 is a metabolic enzyme in the liver, not part of the cGMP-generating pathway.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nitric oxide synthase produces nitric oxide; it does not convert GTP to cGMP.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Phosphodiesterase type 5 degrades cGMP rather than producing it.

questions.topicName: PDE-5 Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man asks his physician for an erectile dysfunction medication that will give him the largest possible window of time for sexual activity after a single dose. Which of the following PDE-5 inhibitors has the longest duration of action, up to 36 hours?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All four have an equal duration of action

choices.label: B
choices.text: Avanafil

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sildenafil

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tadalafil

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vardenafil

explanation.summary: Tadalafil has the longest duration of action, up to 36 hours, giving the widest window for sexual activity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the four PDE-5 inhibitors, tadalafil has the longest time frame of efficacy, up to 36 hours, which gives the patient a much larger window for sexual activity relative to the others.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The durations differ substantially, ranging from about 4 hours for sildenafil to 36 hours for tadalafil.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Avanafil has a duration of action of about 6 hours.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sildenafil has a duration of action of about 4 hours, the shortest of the group.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vardenafil has a duration of action of about 7 hours.

questions.topicName: PDE-5 Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man taking sublingual nitroglycerin for angina also took sildenafil earlier the same evening. He now presents with lightheadedness and a blood pressure of 78/44 mm Hg. Which of the following best explains this dangerous interaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct vasoconstriction of coronary arteries causing ischemia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excessive increase in cardiac contractility raising myocardial oxygen demand

choices.label: C
choices.text: Induction of CYP3A4 that accelerates nitrate metabolism

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reflex tachycardia that raises cardiac output and blood pressure

choices.label: E
choices.text: Synergistic increases in cGMP producing profound vasodilation

explanation.summary: Nitrates and PDE-5 inhibitors act synergistically to raise cGMP, causing profound vasodilation and hypotension.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nitrates are converted to nitric oxide and raise cGMP, while PDE-5 inhibitors prevent cGMP breakdown. Together they act synergistically to cause significant vasodilation and ultimately dramatic reductions in blood pressure, so the two classes should never be taken at the same time.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both drugs cause vasodilation, not coronary vasoconstriction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The interaction lowers blood pressure through vasodilation; it does not primarily increase cardiac contractility.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The dangerous effect is a pharmacodynamic synergy on cGMP and blood pressure, not accelerated nitrate metabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The hallmark of this interaction is hypotension from vasodilation, not a compensatory rise in blood pressure.

questions.topicName: PDE-5 Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man taking a PDE-5 inhibitor for erectile dysfunction reports new indigestion and a burning sensation of acid coming back up into his throat. Which of the following best explains this adverse effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delayed gastric emptying causing food to remain in the stomach

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct erosion of the gastric mucosa by the drug

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased secretion of gastric acid by parietal cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Overproduction of cGMP within the gastric wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter

explanation.summary: Dyspepsia from PDE-5 inhibitors results from relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter and acid reflux.
explanation.whyCorrect: PDE-5 inhibitors relax smooth muscle, including the lower esophageal sphincter. This relaxation allows gastric acid to reflux into the esophagus, producing dyspepsia (indigestion or upset stomach).

whyWrongByChoice.A: The brick attributes dyspepsia to lower esophageal sphincter relaxation, not delayed gastric emptying.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The mechanism is smooth muscle relaxation and reflux, not direct erosion of the gastric mucosa.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dyspepsia here is due to reflux from sphincter relaxation, not increased acid secretion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The symptom results from smooth muscle relaxation permitting reflux, not from local overproduction of cGMP in the stomach.

questions.topicName: PDE-5 Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 47-year-old man who took a PDE-5 inhibitor several hours ago now has a painful erection that has persisted for more than 4 hours. This finding represents which of the following adverse effects, for which he should seek prompt medical attention?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dyspepsia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dysuria

choices.label: C
choices.text: Flushing

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hypotension

choices.label: E
choices.text: Priapism

explanation.summary: An erection lasting more than 4 hours is priapism, a medical emergency requiring prompt attention.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients taking PDE-5 inhibitors should be aware of priapism, an erection lasting over 4 hours. If this occurs the patient should seek medical attention, as it often requires a procedure to drain blood from the corpus cavernosum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dyspepsia is indigestion from lower esophageal sphincter relaxation, not a prolonged erection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Dysuria (painful urination) is not the adverse effect described and is not a recognized effect of these drugs here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Flushing is a common mild vasodilatory effect, not a prolonged painful erection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hypotension is low blood pressure from vasodilation, unrelated to the duration of an erection.

questions.topicName: PDE-5 Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man with chronic stable angina and a prior myocardial infarction takes isosorbide mononitrate 60 mg daily. At a follow-up visit he reports erectile dysfunction over the past year and asks about medication. Which of the following is the most appropriate recommendation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Avoid PDE-5 inhibitors

choices.label: B
choices.text: Start any PDE-5 inhibitor as long as it is separated from the nitrate by 2 hours

choices.label: C
choices.text: Start sildenafil at a low dose taken at the same time as his nitrate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Start tadalafil because its long half-life makes it safest with nitrates

choices.label: E
choices.text: Start vardenafil since it is not affected by fatty meals and avoids interactions

explanation.summary: PDE-5 inhibitors are contraindicated in patients receiving any form of nitrate due to profound hypotension.
explanation.whyCorrect: PDE-5 inhibitors and nitrates act synergistically to cause dramatic reductions in blood pressure. Because this patient takes isosorbide mononitrate, PDE-5 inhibitors should not be prescribed; they must not be used concurrently with any form of nitrate.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A 2-hour separation is insufficient; no PDE-5 inhibitor should be used within 24 hours of nitrate therapy, and longer for tadalafil.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Taking sildenafil at the same time as a nitrate is exactly the dangerous combination that must be avoided.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Tadalafil is not safer with nitrates; its prolonged half-life actually means an even longer interval is needed before a nitrate can be given.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The food effect is irrelevant; vardenafil is still contraindicated with nitrates because of the hypotension risk.

questions.topicName: PDE-5 Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 59-year-old man who takes sildenafil is prescribed clarithromycin, a macrolide antibiotic that inhibits CYP3A4, for a respiratory infection. Which of the following is the most likely consequence of this combination?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complete inactivation of sildenafil before it reaches the circulation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion of sildenafil into an active nitrate metabolite

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enhanced or prolonged sildenafil effect due to reduced metabolism

choices.label: D
choices.text: No interaction because sildenafil is eliminated only by the kidneys

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced sildenafil effect due to enzyme induction

explanation.summary: CYP3A4 inhibitors reduce metabolism of sildenafil, enhancing or prolonging its effect.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sildenafil, tadalafil, and vardenafil are metabolized via CYP3A4, and their effects may be enhanced or prolonged in patients who receive inhibitors of this enzyme. Macrolide antibiotics such as clarithromycin are common CYP3A4 inhibitors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Inhibiting CYP3A4 increases drug exposure rather than inactivating the drug before it reaches the circulation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: PDE-5 inhibitors are not converted into nitrate metabolites; the interaction is a reduction in metabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Although renal dose adjustment applies, sildenafil is metabolized by CYP3A4, so this metabolic interaction is clinically important.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A CYP3A4 inhibitor slows metabolism and increases drug levels; it does not induce the enzyme or reduce the effect.

questions.topicName: PDE-5 Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with chronic kidney disease needs treatment for erectile dysfunction. His physician notes that all PDE-5 inhibitors are eliminated renally and require dose adjustment, but one is of particular concern for toxicity from accumulation because of its prolonged half-life. Which drug is this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Avanafil

choices.label: B
choices.text: None of them require renal dose adjustment

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sildenafil

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tadalafil

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vardenafil

explanation.summary: Tadalafil's long half-life makes it the most concerning for accumulation and toxicity in renal impairment.
explanation.whyCorrect: All PDE-5 inhibitors are eliminated renally, so doses must be lowered when renal function is decreased. Tadalafil, because of its long half-life, is the most concerning for toxicity due to accumulation in patients with altered kidney function.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Avanafil has a duration of about 6 hours and a rapid onset; it is not the primary accumulation concern.
whyWrongByChoice.B: All of the PDE-5 inhibitors are eliminated renally and require dose reduction in renal impairment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sildenafil has a much shorter duration of action (about 4 hours) and is less prone to accumulation than tadalafil.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vardenafil has a duration of about 7 hours and is not the drug singled out for accumulation risk.

questions.topicName: PDE-5 Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 54-year-old man who frequently eats high-fat meals wants a PDE-5 inhibitor whose absorption will not be reduced by fatty food. Which of the following best fits this requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All PDE-5 inhibitors are equally reduced by fatty meals

choices.label: B
choices.text: Avanafil

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sildenafil

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tadalafil

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vardenafil

explanation.summary: Among the four PDE-5 inhibitors, only tadalafil's absorption is not affected by a fatty meal.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the comparison of PDE-5 inhibitors, the absorption of sildenafil, vardenafil, and avanafil is reduced by fatty meals, whereas tadalafil is not affected by fatty meals.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tadalafil is the exception whose absorption is not reduced by fatty meals, so they are not all equal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Avanafil absorption is reduced by a fatty meal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sildenafil absorption is reduced by a fatty meal.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vardenafil absorption is reduced by a fatty meal.

questions.topicName: PDE-5 Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man starting a PDE-5 inhibitor asks what side effects he is most likely to notice. Which of the following are the most common adverse effects of this drug class, all caused by vasodilation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bradycardia, constipation, and dry mouth

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cough, wheezing, and bronchospasm

choices.label: C
choices.text: Headache, flushing, and dizziness

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hypertension, tremor, and insomnia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Weight gain, edema, and hyperglycemia

explanation.summary: The most common adverse effects of PDE-5 inhibitors are headache, flushing, and dizziness from vasodilation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Similar to the nitrate medications, the most common adverse effects associated with PDE-5 inhibitors are headache, flushing, and dizziness, all resulting from the vasodilation these drugs cause.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bradycardia, constipation, and dry mouth are not the vasodilatory effects described for PDE-5 inhibitors.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cough and bronchospasm are not the common adverse effects taught for this class.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PDE-5 inhibitors cause hypotension rather than hypertension because of vasodilation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Weight gain, edema, and hyperglycemia are not associated with PDE-5 inhibitors in this brick.

questions.topicName: PDE-5 Inhibitors

questions.stem: Before its use in erectile dysfunction was discovered, sildenafil was first studied and used as a mainstay of treatment for another condition, with erections noted as a side effect during those trials. For which condition was sildenafil originally studied?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Benign prostatic hyperplasia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chronic stable angina

choices.label: C
choices.text: Congestive heart failure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Essential (systemic) hypertension

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pulmonary arterial hypertension

explanation.summary: Sildenafil was first studied for pulmonary arterial hypertension, where its erectile side effect was noticed.
explanation.whyCorrect: PDE-5 inhibitors are a mainstay of treatment for pulmonary arterial hypertension. Sildenafil was first studied for this indication, and male patients were found to experience erections as a side effect, which led to its use in erectile dysfunction.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Benign prostatic hyperplasia is not the original indication described for sildenafil in this brick.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Chronic stable angina is treated with nitrates, not with the original sildenafil indication described here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Congestive heart failure is not the condition for which sildenafil was first studied.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sildenafil was studied for pulmonary arterial hypertension, not essential systemic hypertension.

questions.topicName: PDE-5 Inhibitors

questions.stem: A 17-year-old girl with severe pustular acne is started on oral doxycycline. Which of the following best describes how this drug interferes with bacterial protein synthesis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blocks aminoacyl-tRNA entry at the 30S acceptor site

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blocks transpeptidation by binding the 50S subunit

choices.label: C
choices.text: Causes misreading by binding 16S rRNA of the 30S subunit

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibits early-phase synthesis by binding the 50S subunit

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prevents initiation complex formation at the 23S rRNA

explanation.summary: Tetracyclines bind the 30S subunit and keep aminoacyl tRNA out of the A site.
explanation.whyCorrect: Doxycycline is a second-generation tetracycline. Tetracyclines bind reversibly to the 30S subunit and block access of aminoacyl tRNA to the A (acceptor) site, halting protein synthesis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Blocking transpeptidation at the 50S subunit describes chloramphenicol, macrolides and clindamycin, not a 30S agent like doxycycline.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Disrupted proofreading and misreading through 16S rRNA is the aminoglycoside mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibition of the early phase at the 50S subunit describes dalfopristin, a streptogramin.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Blocking the initiation complex via 23S rRNA is linezolid's mechanism.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A hospitalized man with a serious infection receives intravenous gentamicin. Unlike most antibiotics that act on the bacterial ribosome, this drug kills the organism rather than only halting its growth. Which of the following best explains this killing effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blockade of the first peptide bond at the 23S rRNA

choices.label: B
choices.text: Faulty proteins inserted into the cell envelope cause lysis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibition of transpeptidation by the 50S subunit

choices.label: D
choices.text: Release of incomplete peptides from the 50S subunit

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reversible blockade of the 30S acceptor site that halts growth

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides are bactericidal because mistranslated proteins disrupt the bacterial membrane.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aminoglycosides target 16S rRNA and disrupt translational proofreading, so incorrect amino acids are incorporated. Some mistranslated proteins are inserted into the bacterial cell membrane, causing lysis, which makes aminoglycosides bactericidal while most PSIs are bacteriostatic.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Blocking the first peptide-bonding step at 23S rRNA is linezolid's mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibition of transpeptidation at the 50S subunit is chloramphenicol's mechanism, which is bacteriostatic.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Release of incomplete proteins after 50S binding describes macrolides and clindamycin, which are mostly bacteriostatic.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reversible A-site blockade is the tetracycline mechanism and is bacteriostatic, not killing.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A medical student reviewing antibiotic classes wants to identify an agent that binds the large ribosomal subunit of bacteria. Which of the following drugs fits this description?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amikacin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Erythromycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Minocycline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Streptomycin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tobramycin

explanation.summary: Macrolides such as clarithromycin are 50S inhibitors; aminoglycosides and tetracyclines are 30S ('Buy AT 30').
explanation.whyCorrect: The 50S (large subunit) inhibitors include the macrolides azithromycin, clarithromycin and erythromycin, along with clindamycin, streptogramins, chloramphenicol and linezolid ('CEL at 50').

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amikacin is an aminoglycoside, which binds the 30S (small) subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Minocycline is a tetracycline, which binds the 30S subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Streptomycin is an aminoglycoside, a 30S inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tobramycin is an aminoglycoside, a 30S inhibitor.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A patient asks why an antibiotic that blocks protein production in bacteria does not shut down protein production in her own cells. Which of the following best explains this selectivity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Human cells exclude the drugs with efflux pumps

choices.label: B
choices.text: Human cytoplasm degrades these drugs rapidly

choices.label: C
choices.text: Human ribosomes lack 30S and 50S subunits

choices.label: D
choices.text: Human ribosomes lack an acceptor site

choices.label: E
choices.text: Human translation does not use transfer RNA

explanation.summary: PSIs are selective because their 30S and 50S targets are absent from eukaryotic ribosomes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Prokaryotes have 70S ribosomes built from 30S and 50S subunits. Eukaryotic ribosomes are not composed of 30S or 50S subunits, so PSIs do not affect host protein synthesis, though they can still have toxic effects.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Efflux pumps are a bacterial resistance mechanism, not the basis for sparing host protein synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Selectivity is explained by the target, not by rapid degradation of the drug in host cytoplasm.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Eukaryotic ribosomes also have tRNA-binding sites; selectivity comes from subunit structure, not absence of an A site.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Human translation does use tRNA; this is not why the drugs spare host cells.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A gram-positive isolate that was susceptible to erythromycin acquires a gene that methylates its 23S ribosomal RNA, and it becomes erythromycin-resistant. Which of the following agents is most likely to lose activity against this isolate as well?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gentamicin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Linezolid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tobramycin

explanation.summary: erm methylation of 23S rRNA causes cross-resistance to macrolides and clindamycin.
explanation.whyCorrect: erm (erythromycin ribosome methylation) genes, transferred among gram-positive bacteria, alter the 23S rRNA. Because the MLS family shares this target site, resistance extends from macrolides to clindamycin, a lincosamide.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Doxycycline binds the 30S subunit, a different target from the altered 23S rRNA site.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gentamicin targets 16S rRNA in the 30S subunit and is not affected by erm methylation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Linezolid's unique binding site leaves it free of the cross-resistance that affects other PSIs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tobramycin is an aminoglycoside acting on the 30S subunit, not on the methylated 50S site.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A 78-year-old man with a markedly reduced glomerular filtration rate requires tobramycin for a serious gram-negative infection. The team chooses lower target serum concentrations than usual. Which property of this drug most directly explains this adjustment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is cleared by hepatic metabolism

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is excreted mainly through the bile

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is excreted unchanged in the urine

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is highly bound to plasma proteins

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is stored in lipid-rich body tissues

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides are excreted unchanged in urine, so impaired filtration calls for lower targets.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aminoglycosides are not substantially metabolized and are eliminated unchanged by the kidneys. With reduced kidney function they accumulate, and because of their narrow therapeutic index lower serum concentrations are targeted in elderly patients and those with renal disease.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hepatic metabolism describes the 50S PSIs; aminoglycosides are not substantially metabolized.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Biliary excretion describes tetracyclines, not aminoglycosides.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aminoglycosides have low protein binding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Aminoglycosides are hydrophilic; lipophilic tissue distribution describes tetracyclines.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man develops a central nervous system infection after neurosurgery. The organism has become resistant to several ribosome-targeting antibiotics through ribosomal methylation and drug export pumps. The team wants a protein synthesis inhibitor that reaches the cerebrospinal fluid readily and is unaffected by cross-resistance. Which of the following is the best choice?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Linezolid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tobramycin

explanation.summary: Linezolid combines CSF entry with freedom from PSI cross-resistance.
explanation.whyCorrect: Linezolid binds the 23S rRNA at the 30S-50S interface, a unique site that keeps it free of cross-resistance with other PSIs. It also has excellent bioavailability and readily enters the CSF.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Macrolides penetrate the CSF poorly without meningeal inflammation and are lost to 23S methylation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Clindamycin has little CSF penetration and shares the MLS site that methylation alters.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tetracyclines have minimal CSF penetration and are susceptible to efflux pumps.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Aminoglycosides have minimal CSF penetration and require IV or IM dosing with close monitoring.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A bacterial isolate resistant to tetracycline is found to carry the tetA gene. The encoded protein sits in the cell membrane. Which of the following best describes how this protein produces resistance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acetylates the drug so it cannot bind the ribosome

choices.label: B
choices.text: Degrades the drug inside the bacterial cytoplasm

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exports drug from the cytoplasm in exchange for protons

choices.label: D
choices.text: Methylates the 23S ribosomal RNA to lower the drug's affinity

choices.label: E
choices.text: Phosphorylates the drug to alter its structure

explanation.summary: TetA is a proton-antiport efflux pump that removes tetracycline from the cytoplasm.
explanation.whyCorrect: TetA is an antiport efflux pump in the cell membrane that transports tetracycline out of the cell while transporting protons in. Because PSIs must reach the ribosome in the cytoplasm, export reduces their activity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acetylation is an enzymatic inactivation used by gram-negative organisms against aminoglycosides.
whyWrongByChoice.B: TetA does not degrade the drug; it removes it from the cell intact.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methylation of 23S rRNA is the erm mechanism of macrolide and clindamycin resistance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Phosphotransferases inactivate drugs enzymatically; TetA is a transporter, not an enzyme.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A student asks why gentamicin for a serious systemic infection is given intravenously rather than as an oral tablet. Which of the following best explains this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Active efflux back into the intestinal lumen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Extensive first-pass metabolism by the liver

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rapid inactivation by acidic gastric contents

choices.label: D
choices.text: Strong lipophilicity that traps it within the gut wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sugar-rich structure that makes it highly hydrophilic

explanation.summary: Aminoglycosides are hydrophilic and poorly absorbed orally, so they are given IV or IM.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aminoglycosides are amino sugars bonded to an aminocyclitol nucleus. Their sugar moieties make them highly hydrophilic and poorly absorbed orally, so they are given IV or IM.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Poor absorption of aminoglycosides is due to their polarity, not intestinal efflux.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aminoglycosides are not substantially metabolized; first-pass metabolism is not the issue.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Instability at gastric pH limits some macrolides, not aminoglycosides.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aminoglycosides are hydrophilic, not lipophilic.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A 66-year-old woman is admitted and started on amikacin for a serious infection. Because the drug's effective and toxic concentration ranges overlap, the team sets up routine monitoring every 1 to 3 days. Which of the following monitoring plans is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complete blood count with visual acuity assessment

choices.label: B
choices.text: Liver enzymes with complete blood count assessment

choices.label: C
choices.text: Liver enzymes with periodic hearing and balance assessment

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum creatinine with hearing and balance assessment

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum creatinine with visual acuity assessment

explanation.summary: Aminoglycoside monitoring uses serum creatinine plus vestibular and auditory assessment.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aminoglycosides have a narrow therapeutic index. Toxicity is monitored every 1-3 days with serum creatinine and the patient's subjective assessment of vestibular and auditory function.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Neither a blood count nor vision is the monitored parameter for aminoglycoside toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: These do not track the kidney, vestibular or auditory toxicity monitored for aminoglycosides.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aminoglycosides are renally eliminated unchanged; liver enzymes are not the monitored parameter.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serum creatinine is right, but the subjective assessment is of vestibular and auditory, not visual, function.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A gram-negative organism causing a health care-associated pneumonia produces an enzyme that transfers an acetyl group onto gentamicin. Which of the following is the direct consequence of this modification?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The 23S rRNA is methylated to reduce binding

choices.label: B
choices.text: The drug becomes bound at the 50S subunit instead

choices.label: C
choices.text: The drug can no longer bind its 16S rRNA target

choices.label: D
choices.text: The drug is converted to a bacteriostatic form

choices.label: E
choices.text: The drug is pumped out across the cell membrane

explanation.summary: Acetylation of aminoglycosides blocks their interaction with 16S rRNA.
explanation.whyCorrect: Bacteria can inactivate PSIs enzymatically. Gram-negative organisms causing health care-associated infections can acetylate aminoglycosides, preventing their interaction with 16S rRNA.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Methylation of 23S rRNA is target site alteration affecting macrolides and clindamycin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Acetylation does not redirect the drug to a different subunit; it prevents ribosomal interaction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The modified drug is inactivated, not converted to a weaker static agent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Efflux is a separate resistance mechanism; acetylation alters the drug itself.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A combination product contains two antibiotics that each bind the 50S ribosomal subunit and together kill the bacterium. Which of the following best describes how the two components work together?

choices.label: A
choices.text: One binds the 30S subunit and the other binds the 50S subunit

choices.label: B
choices.text: One blocks the A site and the other blocks the E site

choices.label: C
choices.text: One causes misreading and the other halts elongation

choices.label: D
choices.text: One inhibits the early phase and the other the late phase

choices.label: E
choices.text: One removes efflux pumps and the other binds the 23S rRNA

explanation.summary: Dalfopristin (early phase) and quinupristin (late phase) act synergistically at the 50S subunit.
explanation.whyCorrect: The streptogramins dalfopristin and quinupristin both bind the 50S subunit. Dalfopristin inhibits the early phase of protein synthesis and quinupristin the late phase, and their synergistic action disrupts peptide-chain assembly and leads to cell death.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Both dalfopristin and quinupristin bind the 50S subunit.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The streptogramins are described by phase of synthesis, not A-site versus E-site blockade.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Misreading through 16S rRNA is an aminoglycoside action, not a streptogramin action.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Neither streptogramin acts on efflux pumps; both bind the ribosome.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitor-1 of 2: Mechanisms of Action

questions.stem: A 3-day-old infant born at 31 weeks' gestation is treated in the neonatal intensive care unit with an antibiotic for a serious infection. Two days later, the infant becomes hypotensive and develops an ashen-gray, cyanotic appearance. Which drug most likely caused this reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azithromycin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chloramphenicol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Clindamycin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Linezolid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Quinupristin/dalfopristin

explanation.summary: Hypotension plus cyanosis in a (premature) newborn given an antibiotic = chloramphenicol gray baby syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gray baby syndrome is specific to chloramphenicol. Newborns, especially premature infants, lack UDP-glucuronosyltransferase to metabolize the drug, and the syndrome characteristically presents with hypotension and cyanosis and is potentially fatal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Macrolides cause GI upset, QT prolongation and hepatic problems; they are not linked to this neonatal syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clindamycin causes diarrhea, allergic reaction, neuromuscular blockade and C. difficile colitis, not hypotension with cyanosis in newborns.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Linezolid causes bone marrow suppression, peripheral neuropathy and serotonin syndrome, not this neonatal presentation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptogramins cause arthralgia, myalgia and raised creatinine and bilirubin; they are not linked to this newborn syndrome.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors-2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 16-year-old girl with severe pustular acne begins oral tetracycline. She takes each dose with a glass of milk at breakfast. After 6 weeks there is no improvement. Which mechanism best explains the treatment failure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accelerated hepatic CYP3A4 metabolism

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bacterial efflux induced by lactose

choices.label: C
choices.text: Chelation of the drug by calcium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inactivation of the drug by gastric acid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased renal tubular secretion

explanation.summary: Dairy calcium chelates tetracyclines and blocks their absorption.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tetracyclines bind calcium and other polyvalent cations. Dairy products such as milk and yogurt chelate the drug in the gut so it cannot be absorbed, so dairy should be avoided 1 h before and 2 h after each dose.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CYP3A4 interactions are a macrolide issue (erythromycin, clarithromycin), not the reason tetracycline fails when taken with milk.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nothing in the scenario points to resistance; the problem is that the drug never gets absorbed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Acid is not the issue; dairy cations bind tetracycline and prevent its absorption.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Milk does not speed renal elimination of tetracycline; the interaction occurs in the gut.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors-2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 78-year-old man with chronic kidney disease receives intravenous gentamicin for gram-negative sepsis. On day 6, his serum creatinine has risen from 1.6 to 3.2 mg/dL and urinalysis shows muddy brown granular casts. Which process best explains the renal injury?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibody deposition along glomerular membrane

choices.label: B
choices.text: Crystal precipitation within collecting ducts

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prerenal hypoperfusion from vasoconstriction

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tubular cell accumulation of the drug

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ureteral obstruction from drug-induced fibrosis

explanation.summary: Aminoglycoside nephrotoxicity = proximal tubular accumulation → acute tubular necrosis; risk up with age and renal impairment.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aminoglycosides are filtered at the glomerulus and accumulate in proximal tubular epithelial cells, increasing cell permeability and leading to acute tubular necrosis. Risk is higher with impaired renal function and in the elderly, both present here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gentamicin injury is a direct toxic effect on tubular cells, not an immune-complex glomerular process.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gentamicin does not crystallize in the urine; it is taken up into tubular epithelium.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Prerenal injury would not produce granular casts; the casts indicate tubular necrosis from drug accumulation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Obstruction is not a described aminoglycoside toxicity.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors-2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman completed a prolonged course of intravenous amikacin. She now reports bilateral hearing loss and unsteadiness when walking in the dark. Audiometry confirms high-frequency sensorineural loss. Which outcome is most likely over the next several months?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Auditory and balance deficits both persist

choices.label: B
choices.text: Auditory and balance deficits both resolve

choices.label: C
choices.text: Auditory deficit resolves only with dialysis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Auditory deficit resolves; balance stays poor

choices.label: E
choices.text: Auditory loss persists; balance may improve

explanation.summary: Aminoglycoside ototoxicity: cochlear (hearing) loss is permanent; vestibular (balance) loss can recover.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aminoglycoside ototoxicity results from inhibition of mitochondrial ribosomes in cochlear and vestibular cells, causing cell death. Cochlear cells cannot regenerate, so hearing loss is irreversible, but vestibular cells can regenerate and balance deficits are sometimes reversed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Vestibular cells can regenerate, so balance deficits are sometimes reversed.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cochlear cells killed by the drug cannot regenerate, so hearing loss is permanent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Removing drug does not revive dead cochlear cells; the hearing loss is irreversible.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This reverses the pattern: cochlear damage is irreversible while vestibular damage may recover.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors-2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 47-year-old man with complicated soft-tissue infection is started on intravenous quinupristin/dalfopristin. Which adverse effect is he most likely to experience?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Arthralgia and myalgia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gray-toned cyanosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Irreversible hearing loss

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sun-induced skin reaction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Yellow tooth discoloration

explanation.summary: Streptogramins (quinupristin/dalfopristin): arthralgia and myalgia in >45% of patients.
explanation.whyCorrect: Arthralgia and myalgia are very common with the streptogramins quinupristin/dalfopristin, occurring in more than 45% of patients. The cause is not known.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cyanosis with hypotension is gray baby syndrome from chloramphenicol in newborns.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ototoxicity is the classic aminoglycoside toxicity, not a streptogramin effect.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Photosensitivity is a tetracycline adverse effect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tooth discoloration results from tetracycline binding calcium in developing teeth.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors-2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man who takes simvastatin daily for hyperlipidemia is diagnosed with community-acquired pneumonia. The physician wants to avoid an antibiotic that would raise his statin levels by blocking the hepatic enzyme that clears it. Which antibiotic should be avoided?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amikacin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clarithromycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Linezolid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Quinupristin/dalfopristin

explanation.summary: Clarithromycin/erythromycin inhibit CYP3A4; avoid with simvastatin and lovastatin.
explanation.whyCorrect: Erythromycin and clarithromycin are CYP3A4 substrates and inhibitors. Simvastatin and lovastatin, which are cleared by CYP3A4, should be avoided with these macrolides.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Amikacin is hydrophilic and not hepatically metabolized, so it does not alter statin clearance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tetracycline interactions involve chelation by cations, not inhibition of hepatic enzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Linezolid's key interaction is serotonin syndrome with SSRIs and SNRIs via MAO inhibition, not a statin interaction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptogramins are known for arthralgia, myalgia and raised creatinine and bilirubin, not CYP3A4-mediated statin interactions.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors-2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman with heart failure is treated with oral erythromycin for a respiratory infection. On day 3, she has two episodes of lightheadedness and palpitations. Which ECG finding is most likely related to her antibiotic?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delta wave with short PR

choices.label: B
choices.text: Diffuse ST-segment elevation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Peaked T waves

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prolonged QT interval

choices.label: E
choices.text: Third-degree heart block

explanation.summary: Macrolides prolong the QT interval; caution in cardiovascular disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: Macrolides can prolong the QT interval and increase the risk of arrhythmia. They should be used with caution in patients with cardiovascular disorders and avoided in combination with other agents that increase this risk.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A delta wave reflects an accessory pathway, which is a structural finding unrelated to the antibiotic.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Diffuse ST elevation suggests pericarditis, not a macrolide adverse effect.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Peaked T waves suggest hyperkalemia, which is not an erythromycin effect described here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Complete heart block is not the arrhythmia mechanism attributed to macrolides.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old woman who takes an SNRI for depression is hospitalized with a resistant infection and started on a new antibiotic. Within hours of the first doses she becomes agitated and febrile, with shivering, diarrhea and muscle rigidity. Which antibiotic was most likely given?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chloramphenicol

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clarithromycin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Doxycycline

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gentamicin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Linezolid

explanation.summary: Linezolid (MAO inhibitor) + SSRI/SNRI = serotonin syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Linezolid is a reversible MAO inhibitor. Combined with drugs that raise serotonin, such as SSRIs and SNRIs, it can cause serotonin syndrome, with symptoms from shivering and diarrhea to rigidity, fever and seizures, typically within hours of starting the new drug.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chloramphenicol causes blood dyscrasias and gray baby syndrome, not this reaction with an SNRI.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Clarithromycin interacts through CYP3A4 inhibition and QT prolongation, not by raising serotonin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Doxycycline interacts with polyvalent cations; it does not raise serotonin levels.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Gentamicin causes nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity and rare neuromuscular blockade, not serotonin excess.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy needs 10 days of an oral tetracycline-class antibiotic for an infection with no suitable alternative. His parents are worried about effects on his teeth. Which choice is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any tetracycline at a reduced dose

choices.label: B
choices.text: Doxycycline given for the 10 days

choices.label: C
choices.text: Minocycline given for the 10 days

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tetracycline taken with milk

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tetracycline with calcium carbonate

explanation.summary: Under age 8, tetracyclines are contraindicated except short-term (<21 days) doxycycline.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tetracyclines other than doxycycline deposit in calcifying teeth and bone, causing yellow discoloration and impaired growth, so they are contraindicated under 8 years. Short-term doxycycline (<21 days) in children is acceptable.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lowering the dose does not prevent tetracycline deposition in calcifying teeth and bone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tetracyclines other than doxycycline deposit in calcifying teeth and bone and are contraindicated under age 8.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dairy chelates tetracycline and blocks its absorption; it does not protect teeth.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Calcium antacids chelate tetracycline and impair absorption rather than preventing deposition.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman finishes a course of oral clindamycin for a dental abscess. Ten days later, she develops frequent watery diarrhea, crampy abdominal pain and fever. Colonoscopy shows yellow-white plaques on the colonic mucosa. Which is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bacterial chelation of ingested calcium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clostridioides difficile overgrowth

choices.label: C
choices.text: Drug-induced serotonin excess

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mitochondrial injury of colon cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neuromuscular blockade of gut muscle

explanation.summary: Clindamycin is classically linked to C. difficile pseudomembranous colitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clindamycin's adverse effects include diarrhea, allergic reaction and neuromuscular blockade, and pseudomembranous colitis from Clostridioides difficile overgrowth is often attributed to clindamycin.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chelation is a tetracycline drug-absorption interaction, not a cause of colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Diarrhea occurs in serotonin syndrome, but mucosal plaques and the timing after clindamycin point to colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mitochondrial protein synthesis inhibition explains linezolid and chloramphenicol marrow toxicity, not this colitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Clindamycin can cause neuromuscular blockade, but that would not produce mucosal plaques and fever.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors-2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man treated with chloramphenicol for a resistant infection develops fatigue, bruising and recurrent infections. Blood counts show anemia, thrombocytopenia and granulocytopenia. The toxicity reflects inhibition of mitochondrial protein synthesis in marrow cells. Which downstream change most directly contributes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Antibody-mediated platelet clearance in spleen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deficient UDP-glucuronosyltransferase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excess serotonin from MAO inhibition

choices.label: D
choices.text: Folate depletion from impaired uptake

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced transferrin receptor expression

explanation.summary: Chloramphenicol marrow toxicity: mitochondrial protein synthesis inhibition → ↓ transferrin receptor expression.
explanation.whyCorrect: Chloramphenicol's blood dyscrasias (aplastic anemia, thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia) arise from inhibition of mitochondrial protein synthesis, which decreases transferrin receptor expression, which is important in maintaining iron homeostasis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The lecture attributes chloramphenicol blood cell toxicity to a direct mitochondrial effect, not autoimmune destruction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Lack of this enzyme explains gray baby syndrome in newborns, not marrow toxicity in adults.
whyWrongByChoice.C: MAO inhibition is linezolid's mechanism for serotonin syndrome, not chloramphenicol marrow suppression.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Chloramphenicol marrow toxicity is linked to iron homeostasis via transferrin receptors, not folate.

questions.topicName: Protein Synthesis Inhibitors-2 of 2: Adverse Drug Reaction

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has received oral linezolid for 7 weeks for a chronic bone infection. He now reports burning and numbness in both feet, and his blood counts show new pancytopenia. Which action of the drug best accounts for both findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accumulation in renal tubular cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antagonism of acetylcholine receptors

choices.label: C
choices.text: Blockade of mitochondrial ribosomes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibition of hepatic CYP3A4

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reversible inhibition of MAO

explanation.summary: Linezolid marrow suppression and peripheral neuropathy come from mitochondrial protein synthesis inhibition.
explanation.whyCorrect: Linezolid's adverse effects include bone marrow suppression, peripheral neuropathy and serotonin syndrome. The marrow suppression and peripheral neuropathy are due to linezolid's inhibition of mitochondrial protein synthesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tubular accumulation is the aminoglycoside nephrotoxicity mechanism and would not cause neuropathy and pancytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Acetylcholine receptor antagonism causes neuromuscular blockade (aminoglycosides, clindamycin), not neuropathy with marrow failure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CYP3A4 inhibition is a macrolide interaction and causes no direct marrow or nerve toxicity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Linezolid does inhibit MAO, but that causes serotonin syndrome, not neuropathy and marrow suppression.
